annotatedSteps.description: Scientific reason for the blue appearance of the sky
annotatedSteps.studentWork: The sky looks blue because the blue colour of the sea water is reflected by the sky.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Incorrect. The blue color of the sky is caused by Rayleigh scattering of sunlight by molecules in the atmosphere, not by reflection of sea water.
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: The molecules of air and other fine particles in the atmosphere have a size smaller than the wavelength of visible light. They scatter light of shorter wavelengths at the blue end much more effectively than light of longer wavelengths at the red end. When sunlight passes through the atmosphere, the fine particles scatter the blue colour more strongly, and this scattered blue light enters our eyes.

teacherNote: Marked against: Mentioning scattering of sunlight by fine air molecules/particles in the atmosphere (1); Explaining that blue light has a shorter wavelength and is scattered much more strongly than red/longer wavelengths / entering our eyes (1). The sky appears blue due to the scattering of sunlight by atmospheric molecules, not reflection from the ocean. Remember that fine particles scatter shorter wavelengths (blue light) much more strongly than longer wavelengths.
